subject.title: feat: sleep tool — pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core `sleep` tool, and should it be a dedicated gateway resume primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted `agentTurn` with explicit sandbox and profile policy?
rationale: This changes the model-facing core tool surface and crosses session-state, cron, interruption, restart, and sandbox boundaries, so automation cannot choose the permanent product/API and security semantics.

options.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
options.body: Accept the feature direction but require same-session wake targeting, interrupt/restart proof, catalog/profile/docs alignment, and explicit sandbox policy before merge.

options.title: Keep existing cron and yield surfaces
options.body: Reject the new core tool for now and keep delayed work on cron, process completion wakes, and `sessions_yield` where ownership already exists.

options.title: Narrow to an extension seam
options.body: Ask for an optional plugin/runtime API seam if maintainers want self-pause behavior outside the default core tool surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction but require same-session wake targeting, interrupt/restart proof, catalog/profile/docs alignment, and explicit sandbox policy before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent runtime, cron, and tool-surface history makes this the strongest available owner for the product/API choice.
